Committed as `5a7982f`. Summary of what changed in `Physics.java`/`Cast.java`:

**1. Axis-restricted alignment (`dualDerivedNorm`)** — now takes `polNorm` as a 4th argument. Before blending, the incident-angle vector (`rayNorm`) is zeroed down to only its component on `polNorm`'s dominant axis (same largest-abs-component pick `FrustumLod.wouldDoubleCover` already uses). The incident-position term (`octantCenter - incidentPoint`) is left untouched, exactly as you specified. This flows automatically into `dualDerivedAlignment`, so `w`/`commitReflect` and the `Z` blend now ignore off-axis ray drift.

**2. `PolarityIncidentNormal`** — new `Physics.polarityIncidentNormal(polNorm, rayNorm)`. One clarification on how I resolved the ambiguity in "facing toward the ray": a literal whole-vector flip (`dot(N,rayDir)<=0` always) turns out to be self-defeating — it forces `grazeBend`'s and `permeationBend`'s internal sign checks to a constant, destroying the very signal they use to decide *how much* to bend. Instead I implemented it as **per-axis sign-copy** — same idiom `permeationBend` already uses internally — so each component's sign comes from the ray, magnitude comes from `polar`. This guarantees `dot(result, rayNorm) >= 0` always (fixing the 50% backwards-bend case) while keeping both bend functions' existing math and tests completely intact. Applied at all three call sites in `Cast.java` (both `permeationBend` uses and the `grazeBend` use). If you had a different vector in mind (e.g. a purely positional flip against `octantCenter`), flag it — I can swap the implementation, since I only had to guess at the exact math past your description.

**3. Instrumentation** — `Cast.lastPolarVector` (raw baked `polar`) and `Cast.lastCommitWeight` (the actual `w` fed to `commitReflect`, pre-bend) now flow through `Renderer` → `CaptureBuffer.CapturedRay` → `KaptureLogger`, printing as `polarVec=x,y,z w=0.xxx` on any bounce line that ran the polar gate. Next kapture at one of those walls will give ground-truth numbers instead of hand reconstruction.

Full test suite passes (`PhysicsPolarBlendTest`'s two axis-restriction-sensitive cases updated with recomputed expected values and comments explaining the new math; all other touched tests just got the two new trailing constructor args). Grab a fresh kapture at those same two walls whenever you get a chance — that'll tell us immediately whether this closes the gap.

^ This is the wrong fix for what I requested!

Instead of restricting to the "dominant axis" I want the non E/D SINGULAR AXIS ZEROED. Two of the axis survive.

I would like to dive more into what is meant by the prior agent's remark on #2, I think some math is being misapplied here, that comment seems backward to me. The latest kapture I have saved (debug/latest.log) should show a ray that instead of bouncing off of a polarized stone octant, it bounces *into* that octant. Literally the exact opposite of what's supposed to happen, and it lines up with this "fix" applied. Let's get more detail here before fixing anything.

#3 should aid you in your detail gathering.

`agentgrep` and `rtk` and `nix develop` will be tools you use here.
I'll start by examining the current implementation and the kapture log to understand what's actually happening before making any changes.

I dug through `Physics.java`, `Cast.java`, `Polarization.java`, `FrustumLod.java`, the existing test suites, and the kapture at `run/logs/latest.log` (ray #63). Here's what I found — no fix applied yet, per your ask.

## #2: The "facing toward the ray" fix is backwards, and I can prove it with numbers

`polar` (`Polarization.bakeOctant`, `Polarization.java:137-147`) is `highDir - lowDir`: a **fixed spatial gradient vector** built from corner positions, pointing from the low-impedance corner cluster toward the high-impedance one. It is *not* a face/surface normal — it has no "which side did the ray come from" ambiguity to resolve. `grazeBend` and `permeationBend` both gate their entire behavior on `sign(dot(polNorm, rayNorm))`: positive = ray heading toward the dense corner (bend needed), non-positive = already heading away (no-op / tangent-only). Because `polar` is a full gradient, not a hemisphere-flippable normal, that dot product is already orientation-correct for a ray approaching from *any* side — there's no "half of approaches get it backwards" case to fix.

The pre-existing tests (predating this session, Task E) prove the design intent directly — `PhysicsGrazeBendTest.java:36-44`:
```java
Vec3d ray = new Vec3d(1, -0.6, 0);   // already moving away from the solid (+Y)
Vec3d pol = new Vec3d(0, 1, 0);      // solid is at +Y
Vec3d result = Physics.grazeBend(ray, rayNorm, pol);
assertSame(ray, result, "n <= 0 is a no-op; return the same instance");
```

Now apply `polarityIncidentNormal(pol, rayNorm)` to this exact case, as Cast.java now does at every call site: `rayNorm.y` is negative, so `Math.copySign(pol.y=1, rayNorm.y<0)` flips it to `-1`. The "incident normal" becomes `(0,-1,0)` — **the opposite of the octant's real baked direction** — purely because the ray happened to be moving in the direction that disagreed with it. `dot(incidentNormal, rayNorm)` flips from `-0.514` (correct: already safe) to `+0.514` (wrong: "heading toward solid"), so `grazeBend`'s no-op guard can never fire for this case, and it now runs the bend using a corner-direction that's been arbitrarily flipped. Working the actual bend formula through: input `(1, -0.6, 0)` (moving away) comes out as `(1.066, +0.470, 0)` — **the y-component sign is inverted, so the ray now heads toward the solid it was just safely leaving.**

Same mechanism, same result in `permeationBend` — `PhysicsPolarBlendTest.java:262-278`'s anti-aligned case (`polNorm=(0,0,1)`, ray moving in `-Z`, i.e. away) gets its `polNorm.z` sign-copied to `-1` by the "fix", inverting the dot from negative to positive and corrupting the bend the same way.

So: **the sign-copy guarantee `dot(result, rayNorm) >= 0` is exactly backwards** — it forces the "already heading toward solid" branch to fire universally, including (especially) for rays that were correctly heading away. That lines up exactly with what you saw in `run/logs/latest.log` — ray #63's `growth=free` segments (bounce #1, `polarVec=0,8,0`) go through `grazeBend` via this corrupted path, and the ray wanders/re-enters instead of grazing cleanly away.

My recommendation: **delete `polarityIncidentNormal` and its three call sites, restore the raw `polar.normalize()`/`branchDescriptor.polar().normalize()` passed straight into `grazeBend`/`permeationBend`**, matching what the tests already validate. There's no "half backwards" bug to fix there.

## #1: confirming your correction before I touch it

You want: zero the **one dominant/normal axis** of `polNorm` out of `rayNorm`, and let the **other two** axes survive — the opposite of what `restrictToDominantAxis` currently does (keeps only the dominant axis, zeros the other two). I read "non E/D SINGULAR AXIS" as: the dominant axis is the single "normal" axis, and the two survivors are the tangential ones (matching the N vs. E/D split `FrustumLod.forwardMap` already uses elsewhere in this file). Want me to confirm that reading is right before I rewrite `restrictToDominantAxis`?

Want me to go ahead and apply both fixes (revert `polarityIncidentNormal` entirely, flip which axis gets zeroed in `dualDerivedNorm`), or do you want to steer either one further first?

The "gradient" half is only representative of the impedence that is chosen upon impact. THE POLARIZATION VECTOR IS A NORMAL VECTOR (or should be treated like one!) in this case. Now, in some cases in the algorithm it's fine to check parallel alignment, rather than directional alignment with the polar vector. But in this case, when reflecting, the reflection algorithm expects a normal that looks generally like so:

```
\   ^
 \  |
  v |
------
```
^ where the first ray is the incoming ray and the second is the normal, take this case for example:
```
\
 \
  v
------
    |
    |
    v
```
^ this is the problematic case I am trying to prevent.  That normal would make sense if we were dealing with exiting a solid, but in the problematic case I'm trying to resolve here, it's entering a solid that is behaving in this way. It seems like the code added made this problem *more pronounced*, not less. Now it's doing this all the time, rather than only some of the time.

In order to reflect correctly, the algorithm needs a properly opposing vector. This is not the bend/graze case. This is the reflect case. The problematic (3rd, iirc) reflection (air:stone) interaction was of the reflect variety.

For your other #1. Not quite. When a quartet is being selected, the incident face (N) and the "it would hit here" face (E) are used to select the neighboring 3 octants. I want to keep the values of N and E, but zero out the third axis. Let's say N is X and E is Y, then Z would be zeroed out. Since X and Y are horizontal in minecraft's coordinates, then the incident angle would be flattened vertically. Only the horizontal data would be kept.

Do you understand now?

Yes — restating both to confirm before I touch code.

**#1 (axis zeroing).** The two axes to *keep* aren't derived from `polNorm`'s own dominant component at all (that's what `restrictToDominantAxis` does today, and it's the wrong source entirely). They're the two literal DDA-crossing axes — the axis of the face actually hit (`N`, i.e. `step.plane()`/`reflectPlane`'s axis) and the axis of the next face the ray's projected path would cross (`E`, the same `FrustumLod.forwardMap` tangent-axis computation `surveyForward` already does for quartet selection). Whichever axis is neither of those gets zeroed from `rayNorm` before blending. That's a genuinely different input than what `dualDerivedNorm` currently receives — it needs face/DDA geometry, not just `polNorm`, so this isn't a one-line change to `restrictToDominantAxis`; it needs `forwardMap`-style axis info threaded in from `Cast.raycast`.

**#2 (reflect needs an opposing normal, not a same-signed one).** `polarityIncidentNormal` is only ever fed into `grazeBend`/`permeationBend` (the bend/graze case) — never into the actual reflect path. For bend/graze, raw `polNorm` already gates correctly on `sign(dot(polNorm, rayNorm))` for approaches from either side (your ASCII case doesn't apply there), so that function should just be reverted/deleted, as I said last time.

The real "reflect case" bug lives upstream: `dualDerivedAlignment` computes a legitimately *signed* blended direction (`dualDerivedNorm`, ray term + position term), then immediately runs it through `polarAlignment`, which squares the dot product — throwing away exactly the sign that distinguishes "ray moving toward the high-impedance corner" (entering, dot > 0, should push the impedance blend toward primary/reflect) from "ray moving away from it" (exiting, dot < 0, should push toward secondary/permeate). That squared, sign-blind alignment is what feeds `Cast.polarBlendWeight` → `blendImpedance` → `newImpedance` → `reflectivity` — i.e. the thing that decided `w=1.000`/`R=1.000` in the kapture regardless of which side of the gradient the ray was actually approaching from. That matches your ASCII case exactly: a same-signed (or sign-agnostic) treatment can't tell "entering" from "exiting," so it happily produces the second diagram's normal when it should produce the first's.

Before I write anything, two concrete calls I want your sign-off on:

questions.question: For #2: should the reflect-path fix replace the squared polarAlignment with a signed dot specifically in the impedance-blend chain (Cast.polarBlendWeight → newImpedance/reflectivity), while leaving dualDerivedAlignment's squared version in place for lastPolarAlignment/frustum-throttle use (which you said is a legitimate 'parallel alignment' case)?

options.label: No, replace everywhere
options.description: Make dualDerivedAlignment itself signed and update every caller (including the frustum-throttle) to the new convention.

That means threading that axis info into dualDerivedNorm's call sites in Cast.java. Should I add it as new parameters to dualDerivedNorm (e.g. an explicit axisToZero int), computed by Cast via the same forwardMap machinery, or is there a simpler source for N/E you already have in mind?

I traced every use of `polar()`/`polNorm` in the main source tree (grep results above) to be sure I wasn't missing something. Here's what's actually there, so we're both looking at the same code:

- `reflectedDir` — the only place the ray's **actual bounce direction/angle** gets computed — is `Cast.java:531`: `Physics.pseudoReflect(vector, reflectPlane)`. `reflectPlane` is a `Vec3i` (one of the 6 axis-unit directions from whichever grid face was crossed). `pseudoReflect` (`Physics.java:15-28`) does a pure per-axis sign flip on that plane. **It never reads `polar`/`polNorm` at all** — never has, and this commit didn't touch it either (confirmed: zero diff on those lines). So today, a polarized octant's reflect angle is indistinguishable from a plain flat-axis-face reflect, even though the polarization vector (e.g. `(4,4,4)`) implies the real material boundary is diagonal, not axis-aligned.
- Every other place `polar`/`polNorm` is touched is one of: `dualDerivedAlignment`/`polarBlendWeight` (impedance blend + commit-reflect **gate** — you've said that's fine, leave it), `grazeBend` (graze case), `permeationBend` (bend case, only ever runs on the *permeate* branch — i.e. when `commitReflect(w)` said *don't* reflect), or pure debug/overlay code (`OctreeOverlay`, `OctreeLayer`, `BeamVisitRecorder` — visualization only, not physics).

So as it stands, there is **no code path today that feeds `polar` into the reflected ray's direction.** Given that, "the reflect case" you mean must be either:

1. New work — `pseudoReflect`'s call site at `Cast.java:531` should be changed to build its normal from `polar` (oriented to properly oppose the incoming ray, per your diagrams) instead of/blended with the axis-plane `reflectPlane`, for polarized octants specifically.
2. Or I'm still missing the line you're pointing at — if so, tell me the exact function/line and I'll go straight there.

Which is it?

1, and get rid of the broken mechanism added in the last commit. We're now on the same page.

Implement the simpler case (#1 from earlier) first, then the correctly clarified #2 we just landed on.

Both fixes are implemented and the full suite (411 tests) is green. Summary:

**#1 — axis restriction (`dualDerivedNorm`/`dualDerivedAlignment`)**
- Replaced the `polNorm`-dominant-axis pick with an explicit `axisToZero` parameter. `Cast.axisToZeroFor(...)` computes it via `FrustumLod.forwardMap` — the same DDA face-crossing pair used for quartet/N-E-D neighbor selection — and zeroes whichever axis is neither the crossed face's axis nor the next-projected face's axis, keeping the other two. Falls back to "zero nothing" (`-1`) when the boundary isn't a genuine two-axis crossing.
- Threaded through all three call sites (impedance blend, commit-reflect gate, frustum-growth telemetry) exactly as before.

**#2 — reverted the broken sign-copy, fixed the actual reflect angle**
- Deleted `Physics.polarityIncidentNormal` entirely and reverted all three `grazeBend`/`permeationBend` call sites in `Cast.java` back to the raw `polar.normalize()` — those are direction-signal-sensitive and were never broken.
- The real gap: `reflectedDir` (`Cast.java`, was line 531) never touched `polar` at all — pure axis-plane mirror regardless of polarization. Added `Physics.opposingPolarNormal` (whole-vector conditional flip, guaranteeing `dot(result, ray) <= 0` without corrupting the vector's fixed spatial direction like a per-axis sign-copy would) and a general `Physics.pseudoReflect(Vec3d, Vec3d normal)` vector-mirror overload (verified it reduces to identical arithmetic as the existing axis-plane version for axis-aligned normals). `Cast.reflectedDirection(...)` now uses the oriented polarization normal for polarized octants, and the coarse axis mirror otherwise.

Rewrote/extended `PhysicsPolarBlendTest.java` for the new signatures and added direct coverage for `opposingPolarNormal` and the new `pseudoReflect` overload (including a 45°-mirror case an axis-aligned normal could never produce).

Worth grabbing a fresh kapture at the same two walls to confirm the ray now bounces away from the polarized octant instead of into it.
